title: Running a program
text: prctl renamed the task; running a program names it too, after the program. `execve` replaces the program a process runs: the task stays, with its pid; its memory and its program are new.
1. [do_execveat_common](1:do_execveat_common) opens the file ([do_open_execat](1:do_open_execat)), and [load_wasm_binary](1:load_wasm_binary), this kernel's loader for wasm programs, reads it in.

2. [begin_new_exec](1:begin_new_exec) is the point of no return: [exec_mmap](1:exec_mmap) gives the task new memory (a new `mm_struct`; the old one goes), its signal handlers are reset ([flush_signal_handlers](1:flush_signal_handlers)), and [__set_task_comm](1:__set_task_comm) names it after the program. [What it changed](1:exec_mmap:memory).

3. The call does not return: the new program runs, from its start. Here it is /bin/prog again, the page's program, so it takes the next call, getpid: the same pid as before ([__task_pid_nr_ns](2:__task_pid_nr_ns)).
